name: Bright Strum
description: The treble up and the bass down, the volume low, the supply stiff: strummed chords that cut through a band without breaking up. Put a cabinet after it, such as Boxed Twelves.

name: Chime
description: The brilliant channel through the treble boost with its volume low: clean, bright chords that ring, and a little bite when dug into. Put a cabinet after it, such as Boxed Twelves.

name: Cranked Thirty
description: The brilliant volume at its top, so the power stage clips and the supply sags: thick, compressed chords with the cut halfway to tame the top. Put a cabinet after it, such as Boxed Twelves.

name: Dark Lead
description: The volume high, the treble down, and the cut well up: a round, singing lead with the chime taken off. Put a cabinet after it, such as Boxed Twelves.

name: Edge of Breakup
description: The treble boost with the volume just past noon: chords that clean up with the guitar's volume and grind when hit hard. Put a cabinet after it, such as Boxed Twelves.

name: Jangle
description: The brilliant channel with the treble boost out, as the combo was before it: thin and glassy, for arpeggios and twelve strings. Put a cabinet after it, such as Boxed Twelves.

name: Joined Channels
description: Both jacks joined, as a short cord across them does: the normal channel's body under the treble boost's chime. Put a cabinet after it, such as Boxed Twelves.

name: Normal Channel
description: The normal channel, full and dark beside the brilliant one, with its volume at noon: warm rhythm that starts to break up when hit. Put a cabinet after it, such as Boxed Twelves.
